summary: ⚠️ THE INDEX MOVED DURING THIS REVIEW. I was asked to bind this verdict to 0507fef4838508... and read the whole diff at that hash; by the time I recorded, the staged bytes hashed to 92064ae123dbc4... I diffed the two rather than re-reading, and the delta is exactly two lines, both improvements, neither touching a finding: backlog.md's M4.10c row replaced 'every M4 delta is single-segment so the two placements are byte-equivalent today and only M5 tells them apart' with 'three existing multi-segment fixtures kill the once-per-delta field at T0 ONCE THEY CARRY DIFFERENT TRIPLES' (the test reviewer's round-5 major, now in the row as well as the ADR and notes, and it removes the same over-claim from a third copy); and SPEC.md's T0 matrix row gained the bare-pair mutation in its mutation column. I re-verified after the move that SPEC.md:55/:501/:511, backlog-notes.md and both ADRs are byte-identical to what I read, so every finding below stands verbatim against 92064ae. This verdict is bound to 92064ae, not to the hash I was given. Round 6. Every amendment claimed in the request was verified against the staged bytes and each one holds: SPEC.md scope item 9 (:379-383), acceptance criterion 6 (:394-401), the T0 matrix row (:410) and the M4.10 task row (:419) all carry the triple and the dated ADR-0036 amendment; criterion 6 states the restarted-pod-reissuing-0 case as ACCEPTED and carries the answer-or-refuse bound; the M4.10c notes are rewritten to prescribe the shape the row prescribes; the still-open parent row no longer names the bare pair; both the ADR (:104-108) and the M4.10c notes name the three T0 fixtures that kill the once-per-delta placement and scope the invisibility to PRODUCTION; the 'nothing applied, so a re-flush is safe' parenthetical is gone, correctly, since Sequencer.java:43,86 documents that channel as AMBIGUOUS. Every tree fact the ADR cites was checked and is accurate: applyChain does LIST-with-startAfter then GET (ChainReplay.java:362-383), the Hop javadoc quote is exact (:50), CheckpointWriter's pods.merge comment is exact (:126-129), MAX_KEY_BYTES is 1024, CheckpointTest asserts <64 KiB at 1,600 streams stating ~38 KiB, Checkpoint.VERSION is a strict equality check (:151), the M3.0 quote is faithful, SegmentPublisher's 'put, not putIfAbsent' comment and its instance AtomicLong are as described, and DefaultIngest:349 does consume flushSeq++ before a commit that can throw. Three majors remain, and two of them are the same duplicate-miss the F2 fix was written for. I agree SPEC.md:55/:501/:511 belong to M4.10c -- see finding 5 for the part of that which is not landable as staged.

findings.title: The ADR restates the claim M4.10 rounds 7-9 measured false: 'Nothing on the chain carries pod attribution today'
findings.detail: The CommitDelta bullet reads: 'Nothing on the chain carries pod attribution today (`CheckpointWriter` records this: it is "the only place the writer can see `podId` and `flushSeq`"), so without this a takeover loses every commit made since the predecessor's last checkpoint.' Every SegmentCommit on the chain carries `segmentKey`, which in production is a rendered SegmentKey (`SegmentPublisher.java:133-141`) whose grammar is `<ts>-<podShortId>-<seq>-h<len>-<filter>` (SegmentKey.java:16, :40). podShortId is on the chain. The cited javadoc (CheckpointWriter.java:105-106) says 'podId AND flushSeq', a conjunction, and does not support the flat claim; only flushSeq is absent. The tree already carries the corrected form, bought by three review rounds and recorded in the M4.10 baselines entry this commit sits beside: backlog-notes.md:309 says 'Only `flushSeq` is absent from the chain: `SegmentKey` puts `podShortId` and a per-pod sequence inside the segment key that every `SegmentCommit` carries'. An accepted ADR now contradicts that sentence in the same repository, and outranks it.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10c implements the bullet literally and writes a podId string into every SegmentCommit beside the segmentKey that already encodes podShortId. One SegmentCommit then carries two independent pod attributions with nothing forcing them to agree -- precisely the hazard SegmentCommit's own javadoc cites for rejecting a key per RunCommit ('nothing in that shape would stop two runs of the same segment naming different keys'), reintroduced by the fix for idempotency. The alternative the false premise hides is never weighed: the delta may only need `(incarnationId, flushSeq)` per SegmentCommit, with podId read from the key, at the cost of a `podShortIdOf(key)` accessor SegmentKey does not have today (it exposes only headerLenOf, :212). That is a real choice with a byte cost and a consistency cost on each side, and the ADR forecloses it on a fact that is not true.
findings.suggested_fix: State the tree fact instead, as backlog-notes.md:309 already does: the chain carries podShortId inside every segment key but no `flushSeq` and no incarnation, and nothing parses podShortId back out today. Then say whether the delta carries podId redundantly or derives it, and why.

findings.title: The parent M4.10 notes still say M4.10c is conditional and may be void -- F2 fixed one copy and missed the reachable duplicate
findings.detail: The M4.10c section was rewritten to '⚠️ NO LONGER CONDITIONAL' and the M4.10c row now prescribes the shape. The parent #m410 section, four lines of which this commit did not touch, still reads: 'Order is forced by M4.10b, which decides the key's shape and whether any format changes at all. M4.10c happens only if it does, and may be void. M4.10d is blocked by M4.10b. Its ANCHOR needs no format change ... but how far its dedup reaches depends on M4.10b's answer: returning the original offsets across a takeover needs a carrier for `flushSeq`.' Every clause is falsified by the ADR this commit accepts. This section is not orphaned prose: backlog.md:122's M4.10 row is still `split` and still links to it ([notes](backlog-notes.md#m410)), so it is live guidance. The baselines entry this same commit writes for M4.10a names this exact failure -- 'AND DELETING THE SECTION MISSED ITS DUPLICATE ... fixing one copy of a fact and missing its duplicates' -- and the F2 fix reproduced it one level up.
findings.failure_scenario: A session reaches M4.10c through the parent row (which is the natural route: M4.10 is the `split` banner and the only row that explains the ordering), reads 'M4.10c happens only if it does, and may be void', and either skips the row as possibly-void work or opens it expecting to re-litigate whether a format change is needed at all -- against an accepted ADR that says both formats change. That is the same wasted round M4.10's own rounds 4-6 were spent on.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite backlog-notes.md:184-190 to state what the landed ADR decided: c is unconditional and carries both formats, d is unblocked, and answering across a takeover is bounded by the pointer rather than by 'whatever M4.10b makes durable'.

findings.title: The ADR's own highest-risk clause -- the minting site -- is assigned to no row and named by no test
findings.detail: ADR-0036:41 is emphatic: '⚠️ THE MINTING SITE IS PART OF THE DECISION, not an implementation detail ... Minting per FLUSH instead -- inside `flushLocked` -- makes dedup a total no-op in production while every sequencer-seam test still passes, because those tests supply the incarnation themselves. A test at the seam cannot see this; `IngestCommitPathTest`'s recording sequencer can.' Neither open row carries any of it. M4.10c (backlog.md:123) is scoped to `Checkpoint` and `CommitDelta` -- 'BOTH FORMATS' -- and `CommitRequest` is neither, being an in-process record that is never encoded. M4.10d (:124) is the dedup and the anchor. Neither row, and neither notes section, names `CommitRequest`, `DefaultIngest`, the `ingest` module, or `IngestCommitPathTest`. The omission is conspicuous against the standard these very rows set: M4.10c names three fixtures by filename that kill the once-per-delta placement, and M4.10d names `CheckpointWriterContentTest`'s `doesNotContainKey("poda")` by assertion. The one mutation the ADR says is invisible to the entire sequencer seam is the one with no owner and no named test.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10c adds `incarnationId` to CommitRequest and, needing a value at the only call site, writes `UUID.randomUUID()` inside `flushLocked` beside the existing `flushSeq++` (DefaultIngest.java:349) -- the smallest edit that compiles. Every format test passes because the fixtures supply their own incarnations; every sequencer test passes because BatchingSequencerTest and LocalSequencer tests construct CommitRequests directly. M4.10d then lands the dedup, its whole suite green, and in production no two commits from one pod ever share an incarnation, so `flushSeq <= lastApplied for the same incarnation` never matches and dedup is a total no-op. The tree is green, the acceptance criterion is green, and FR-3 does not hold.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the minting site in whichever row lands `CommitRequest` -- one clause: 'mint `incarnationId` once per `DefaultIngest` instance, not per flush; pinned by `IngestCommitPathTest`'s recording sequencer, which is the only seam that can see it (ADR-0036)'. It costs a sentence and it is the mutation the whole feature turns on.

findings.title: 'No commit-path request scales with pods' is true of detection only, and the ADR's own answer path is the counterexample
findings.detail: Carried from round 5 and recorded for the commit body per that round's recommendation; re-recorded because it is now bold prose in an accepted ADR that later readers will cite. The bold claim covers both halves of the commit path; the sentence supporting it covers only detection ('an in-memory comparison against state recovered once per takeover'). The answer path issues one GET of the pointed delta per detected replay (:119-127), and B replaying pods point at B distinct deltas, so those GETs cannot coalesce.
findings.failure_scenario: A sequencer takeover fails every in-flight commit at once; all B pods retry; the successor detects B replays and issues B uncoalescable GETs. That is legitimate -- pods are nodes, the axis non-negotiable 6 permits, and it is once per takeover, not per record -- but a reader who later needs the true bound finds a flat 'no request scales with pods' and either believes the answer path is free or, worse, deletes the pointer on the strength of it.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the claim: detection scales with nothing; answering costs one GET per detected replay, on the node axis and once per takeover, uncoalescable across pods.

findings.title: The three CommitRequest-shape sites belong to M4.10c -- agreed -- but nothing assigns them, and there are three, not two
findings.detail: I agree with the decision not to touch them here. SPEC.md:55 ('the commit request carries `(podId, flushSeq, segments…)` ... so the record shape does not have to change when the remote implementation lands'), :501 (the Risks row, 'the seam contract carrying `(podId, flushSeq)` from the start') and :511 (the M4.1 task row) describe the seam as it stands today, and ADR-0036 does not falsify them -- if anything it strengthens :55, since an incarnation minted per process is exactly the field that keeps meaning when M5 moves the sequencer out of process, where the rejected lease epoch would not. They become false the moment M4.10c lands. But M4.10c's row and notes name neither the file nor the three lines, so the only thing that would catch them is a reader noticing.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10c lands `incarnationId` in CommitRequest. SPEC.md then tells every subsequent reader, in its scope prose, its Risks table and its task table, that the seam carries `(podId, flushSeq)` -- the pair the milestone's own scope item 9 and criterion 6 now say cannot carry idempotency. check-links and every other gate stay green, because all three are prose. This is the duplicate-miss pattern again, and the third site is the one the request did not name.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to M4.10c's notes: 'and SPEC.md:55, :501 and :511 describe the request as `(podId, flushSeq, …)`; all three move with this row.'

findings.title: The pointer's target has a lifetime this ADR does not own and does not mention
findings.detail: The slot points at `(epoch, sequence)` of a delta, and the ADR's ground for the pointer is that answering would otherwise be 'bounded to the uncheckpointed tail'. Answering is in fact bounded by the pointed delta continuing to exist. roadmap.md:16 gives M7 'GC from the commit log', and the deltas that become collectable first are exactly the ones a checkpoint has absorbed -- which is where a pointer written at the last checkpoint points. The ADR enumerates REFUSE for the case where the pointed delta carries a different triple, but not for the case where it is gone (BinStore has no not-found type on `get`; CheckpointCursor.java:66-70 records what that costs when it is guessed at).
findings.failure_scenario: After M7, a pod retries a commit whose delta was collected. The watermark survives in the checkpoint, so the replay is detected; the GET of the pointed delta fails; the sequencer refuses. DefaultIngest completes the append exceptionally on a flush that actually landed -- the producer-visible-failure-on-a-landed-flush outcome M4.10d's notes single out as the thing not to build. It fails silently in the sense that nothing tests it until M7 exists.
findings.suggested_fix: One clause in Consequences: the pointed delta must outlive the checkpoint slot naming it, which is a constraint on M7's GC; and say what a missing target does (refuse, distinguishably from a mismatching one).

findings.title: The ADR-0033 amendment uses two mechanisms where the adr skill prescribes one, and splits the header block
findings.detail: The adr skill's Staleness section says to record divergence 'as a dated note on the `Status:` line -- never by rewriting the body'. This commit adds the dated Status note AND a five-line ⚠️ banner, and places the banner between `Date:` and `Requirements:`, so ADR-0033 is now the only record in decisions/ whose four header lines are not contiguous. Nothing in the body was rewritten, so the rule's purpose -- not erasing what was believed at decision time -- is met; the mechanism is doubled.
findings.failure_scenario: The next ADR that amends an earlier one copies whichever half it happens to see, and the directory ends up with three amendment conventions. More concretely, the same fact now lives in two places one line apart, and the next amendment to ADR-0033 updates one of them -- the failure mode this project has paid for repeatedly and which the M4.10a baselines entry names by name.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the dated Status note; fold the banner's content into it or move it below the header block so `Status/Date/Requirements/Research` stay contiguous.
